positive.name: GeoVINS
positive.title: GeoVINS: Map-Aided Visual-Inertial Navigation for UAV Geo-Localization
positive.abstract: GeoVINS combines visual-inertial odometry with georeferenced satellite map matching to provide drift-free absolute UAV localization in GNSS-denied environments. Map observations constrain the VIO trajectory and recover global position and heading.

positive.name: NGPS
positive.title: NGPS: GPS-Denied Aerial Geo-Localization and 2.5D Reconstruction via Deep Satellite Image Matching and Multi-Rate Sensor Fusion
positive.abstract: We present NGPS, a visual geo-localization framework for high-altitude UAVs that provides GPS-free absolute positioning by matching down-facing images to georeferenced satellite imagery. It fuses absolute position, VIO and IMU updates and enables georeferenced orthomosaic reconstruction.

positive.name: PiLoT
positive.title: PiLoT: Neural Pixel-to-3D Registration for UAV-based Ego and Target Geo-localization
positive.abstract: PiLoT tackles UAV-based ego and target geo-localization by directly registering a live video stream against a geo-referenced 3D map. It estimates drift-free UAV pose and target geographic coordinates in GNSS-denied environments.

positive.name: PiLoT v2
positive.title: PiLoT v2: Pixel-to-Orthogonal Map Alignment for Free-view UAV Geo-localization
positive.abstract: PiLoT v2 performs direct pixel-to-orthogonal map registration for free-view UAV geo-localization. It uses True Digital Orthophoto Maps and Digital Surface Models as the map substrate and integrates gravity and laser range priors into pose optimization.

positive.name: AeroMap3D
positive.title: AeroMap3D: Anchoring Monocular UAV 6-DoF Localization to Visual-Geometric-Semantic Map Priors
positive.abstract: AeroMap3D anchors onboard UAV imagery to satellite maps, bare-earth digital elevation models and OpenStreetMap priors. Dense UAV-to-map correspondences are lifted onto DEM terrain for RANSAC-PnP 6-DoF pose estimation and fused with relative motion in a delayed-state EKF.

positive.name: RIM
positive.title: RIM: A Retrieval-In-Matching Framework for Cross-Domain Global Visual Localization of UAVs
positive.abstract: Global visual localization of UAVs using remote-sensing reference maps is addressed through cross-view retrieval, local feature matching and geometric verification. Reference views sampled from Google 3D Tiles support robust six-degree-of-freedom pose estimation.

positive.name: Bearing-UAV
positive.title: Beyond Matching to Tiles: Bridging Unaligned Aerial and Satellite Views for Vision-Only UAV Navigation
positive.abstract: Bearing-UAV is a purely vision-driven cross-view navigation method that jointly predicts UAV absolute location and heading from unaligned aerial and satellite views. Bearing-UAV-90k is a multi-city benchmark for cross-view localization and navigation.

positive.name: OffNadirLoc
positive.title: OffNadirLoc: Benchmark and Framework for Challenging UAV-to-Satellite Geo-Localization under Large Off-Nadir Views
positive.abstract: OffNadirLoc is a benchmark and framework for large off-nadir UAV-to-satellite geo-localization. It learns view-invariant features across satellite images and corresponding UAV images and evaluates cross-view retrieval on multiple datasets.

positive.name: Altitude-Adaptive Vision-Only Geo-Localization
positive.title: Altitude-Adaptive Vision-Only Geo-Localization for UAVs in GPS-Denied Environments
positive.abstract: The method matches downward-looking UAV images to georeferenced satellite or aerial map tiles. Relative altitude normalizes scale before visual place recognition and weighted coordinate estimation provides coarse map localization in GPS-denied environments.

positive.name: broad visual place recognition wording
positive.title: Visual Place Recognition for Long-Range Aerial Navigation
positive.abstract: A drone retrieves its location from a large database of georeferenced orthophotos and uses the retrieved coordinates as a global navigation update.

positive.name: broad georeferencing wording
positive.title: Automatic Georeferencing of UAV Imagery via Map Correspondence
positive.abstract: We align airborne camera frames with a geospatial base map to recover camera pose and geographic coordinates without GNSS.

positive.name: broad terrain relative wording
positive.title: Learning Terrain-Relative Navigation from Monocular Aerial Images
positive.abstract: The aircraft matches onboard imagery to an elevation map and estimates global position and heading over long trajectories.

positive.name: broad camera relocalization wording
positive.title: Camera Relocalization against Large-Scale Geospatial Maps
positive.abstract: Queries captured by an unmanned aerial vehicle are registered to a geo-referenced 3D city map for absolute pose estimation.

positive.name: broad aerial image retrieval wording
positive.title: Cross-Domain Aerial Image Retrieval for Global Localization
positive.abstract: Drone observations are retrieved against overhead satellite images, followed by geometric verification and geographic coordinate estimation.

positive.name: broad absolute pose wording
positive.title: Absolute Pose Estimation of Drones from Overhead Maps
positive.abstract: Our system establishes visual correspondences between UAV frames and a georeferenced map to solve the six degree-of-freedom camera pose.

positive.name: traditional UAV SLAM
positive.title: A Lightweight Feature-Based SLAM System for Autonomous Quadrotors
positive.abstract: We present a traditional stereo SLAM pipeline for a quadrotor UAV using geometric feature tracking, local bundle adjustment and loop closure. The system estimates a locally consistent aerial trajectory without a georeferenced map.

positive.name: traditional UAV visual odometry
positive.title: Robust Monocular Visual Odometry for Low-Altitude UAV Flight
positive.abstract: This visual odometry method estimates the relative motion of a drone camera with handcrafted features and geometric optimization in low-texture aerial scenes.

positive.name: traditional UAV VIO
positive.title: Visual-Inertial Odometry for Agile Micro Aerial Vehicles
positive.abstract: A tightly coupled VIO estimator fuses monocular images and IMU measurements onboard a micro aerial vehicle for real-time state estimation without GNSS or a global map.

positive.name: general visual-inertial SLAM
positive.title: Robust Visual-Inertial SLAM with Online Calibration
positive.abstract: We present a general-purpose camera-IMU SLAM system that estimates six-degree-of-freedom pose, trajectory and a sparse map with online spatiotemporal calibration.

positive.name: general visual odometry
positive.title: Direct Sparse Visual Odometry in Dynamic Environments
positive.abstract: The method estimates camera motion and a locally consistent map from monocular image sequences using robust geometric optimization.

negative.name: ordinary remote-sensing detection
negative.title: A Transformer for Small Vehicle Detection in High-Resolution Satellite Images
negative.abstract: This paper proposes an object detector for vehicles in satellite imagery and reports average precision on a remote sensing detection benchmark. It does not estimate camera pose or match UAV observations to a geographic map.

negative.name: ordinary UAV tracking
negative.title: Real-Time Multi-Object Tracking from UAV Videos
negative.abstract: We improve pedestrian detection and tracking in drone video using a lightweight detector. The method does not use a georeferenced map and does not output absolute geographic position.

negative.name: ordinary remote-sensing segmentation
negative.title: Semantic Segmentation of Buildings in Aerial Imagery
negative.abstract: A segmentation network predicts building masks in high-resolution overhead images. It performs land-cover mapping rather than camera localization or UAV-to-map registration.

negative.name: humanoid-specific odometry
negative.title: Kinematic-Inertial-LiDAR-Visual Odometry for Humanoid Robots
negative.abstract: This platform-specific estimator tightly depends on humanoid joint encoders, leg kinematics, IMU, LiDAR and cameras for biped locomotion.
